record.issuing_body: Ministry of Science and ICT (AI Safety and Trust Support Division); also published by the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA) and the National Information Society Agency (NIA)
record.summary: Guidance from the Ministry of Science and ICT on the transparency duties of Article 31 of Korea's AI Basic Act: prior notice that a product or service is operated on the basis of high-impact or generative AI (para. 1); marking that outputs were generated by generative AI (para. 2); and notice or marking of deepfakes, defined as virtual sound, image or video outputs hard to distinguish from reality (text excluded), so that users clearly recognise them (para. 3). The duties fall on the operator that finally provides the product or service to users, including overseas operators affecting Korean nationals. It sets out notice channels and human-perceptible or machine-readable marking methods.
record.notes: Released by the Ministry of Science and ICT on 22 January 2026, when the Act entered into force, under the name 'Guidance on securing AI transparency (guideline)' (인공지능 투명성 확보 안내 지침(가이드라인)); a draft had been published in September 2025. NIA posted a revised file dated 26 January 2026 and recorded a wording change to the service examples for text outputs on 27 January 2026. Under the ministry's policy of a guidance period of at least one year, fact-finding and fines under the transparency provisions are suspended during that period, and the ministry plans to keep revising the guideline. Inside a service, outputs may be marked through the user interface, but outputs that can be downloaded or shared must carry the mark in the output itself; exported deepfakes need a mark that people can perceive intuitively, while artistic and creative works may use a lighter marking that does not hinder their display or enjoyment. Where a machine-readable mark is used, users must be told at least once by text or voice. A foundation-model developer that only supplies an API is not bound; the operator that offers the service to users is. The guideline coins the term 'general outputs' for AI outputs that are not deepfakes.

verification.note: Stored: NIA's copy of the guideline (PDF, 33 pages; the cover page has no text layer, and its image shows the logos of MSIT and TTA); MSIT's press release of 21 January 2026 on korea.kr, as a page (headline, date and attachments) and as a print copy with the full release text; and NIA's post of 22 January 2026 distributing the AI Basic Act guidelines. The guideline confirms the title, the three Article 31 duties, the deepfake definition, the duty holder and the marking rules. The press release confirms the release on 22 January 2026 (distributed 21 January for the morning papers of 22 January), the September 2025 draft, the guidance period of at least one year, the responsible AI Safety and Trust Support Division and publication on the MSIT and TTA websites. NIA's post confirms the file dated 26 January 2026, the change of 27 January 2026 and that the posted files are the current versions. The KOSA help desk's alternative title, cited in an earlier version of this record, is in no stored file and is no longer stated.

judgment.status_reasoning: MSIT's press release says the ministry released (공개하였다) the guideline on 22 January 2026, and NIA's post of 22 January 2026 says the current versions of the AI Basic Act guidelines have been published (현재본이 공개되었습니다); its revision notice of 27 January 2026 is a wording change, not a replacement. The guideline carries no draft marking (the safety guideline, KR-05, does), and no stored file shows a withdrawal. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands; the press release adds that the guideline will keep being supplemented during the guidance period.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope without a scope note: ministry guidance implementing the transparency duty of an AI-specific statute.

changes.date_published: 2026-01-21 to 2026-01-22. 2026-01-21 is the date the press release was distributed (embargoed for the morning papers of 22 January, print copy page 2); the release itself says MSIT released the guideline on 22 January, and NIA posted it on 22 January 2026.
changes.issuing_body: Added TTA: the press release says the guideline is published on the MSIT and TTA websites (print copy page 4), and the cover carries both logos. The AI Safety and Trust Support Division is now supported by the press release's contacts; NIA's distribution by its post.
changes.summary: Rewritten from the Korean text. Deepfake is the guideline's defined term for all para. 3 outputs (sound, image or video hard to distinguish from reality; text excluded, page 9), not an example of them. Added who is bound (page 6). The grace period moved to notes, now from the stored press release.
changes.notes: Removed the press-based sentence ending 'those details were not checked against the full text' (process language); the export-marking rules and the coverage of overseas operators are now stated from the guideline (pages 6, 11 to 13). The September 2025 draft and the guidance period now rest on the stored press release (print copy page 2). Removed the KOSA alternative title, which no stored file supports.
changes.verification: New note saying what each stored file confirms.

open_questions: The KOSA help desk's alternative title '생성형 인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인' was removed for lack of a stored source.
The press release calls the document '인공지능 투명성 확보 안내 지침(가이드라인)', while the guideline's own title is '인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인'; original_title follows the guideline.
